rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant mass: a bent, low-rise bar with a clear hierarchy and a recognizable public cut at the access side. It responds to the parcel better than a generic box because the plan is not just envelope-filling; the curve/bend and the notch create an identifiable open-space figure. The form is coherent across the four views and does not show obvious view-to-view collisions, so it clears the hard geometry gate. That said, the section is still relatively quiet and the public void is modest rather than deeply inhabited, so it is not a strong exemplary court building yet. For neighborhood living, the active ground threshold is legible enough and the mass can plausibly support mixed-use living/program around it, but it would benefit from a slightly clearer carved court or threshold to strengthen ground-publicness and access response. The references support the general language: curved/terraced low-rise masses with central voids and explicit threshold carving. The candidate is less socially expansive than the strongest references, but still program-compatible.
